skill.name: request-refactor-plan
skill.description: Create a detailed refactor plan with tiny commits via user interview, then file it as a GitHub issue. Use when user wants to plan a refactor, create a refactoring RFC, or break a refactor into safe incremental steps.
skill.summary: Turn a refactor request into a scoped, test-aware plan of small commits and a structured GitHub issue.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: No static findings required adjudication, and review of SKILL.md found no prompt injection or malicious intent. The prompt-only workflow contains no executable code or hidden security-sensitive behavior.

content.value_statement: Large refactors often fail because scope, testing, and sequencing remain unclear. This skill inspects the repository and creates an incremental plan for a GitHub issue.
actual_capabilities: Interviews the user about the problem, proposed solution, constraints, and implementation decisions.
Explores the repository to verify assumptions and understand the current design.
Presents alternative approaches before finalizing the solution.
Checks existing test coverage and records testing decisions.
Breaks the refactor into small commits that preserve a working codebase.
Formats the final plan as a structured GitHub issue.
limitations: Requires access to the repository and enough user context to verify assumptions.
Plans the refactor but does not implement the proposed code changes.
Publishing the issue depends on available GitHub access and authentication.
The final issue intentionally excludes file paths and code snippets.

use_cases.title: Plan a Legacy Module Refactor
use_cases.description: Convert an unclear cleanup request into scoped, testable commits that keep the application working.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Architecture RFC
use_cases.description: Compare solution options and document interfaces, contracts, schema changes, and excluded work.

use_cases.title: Review Refactor Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify unresolved decisions, testing gaps, and sequencing risks before work enters the sprint.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a refactor for [component]. The problem is [problem]. Ask me for missing context before proposing commits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the refactor idea is early and needs structure.

prompt_templates.title: Scope a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [repository area]. Verify [assumptions], compare alternatives, and define in-scope and out-of-scope work before creating the plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when scope and approach need agreement.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Test-Aware Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess test coverage for [area], identify behavior to protect, and create tiny commits where every step leaves the codebase working.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when regression risk is significant.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Refactoring RFC
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a GitHub issue for [refactor], covering decisions, interfaces, contracts, migrations, tests, commit sequence, exclusions, and unresolved questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for cross-team or architecture-level refactors.

output_examples.input: Replace duplicated authorization checks with a shared policy service while preserving current behavior.
output: Problem Statement: Authorization rules are duplicated and can diverge.
Solution: Introduce one policy boundary without changing public behavior.
Commits: Capture behavior tests, add the policy service, migrate one caller per commit, then remove duplication.
Out of Scope: New roles, permission redesign, and unrelated endpoint changes.

output_examples.input: Separate billing logic from the web controller and improve its test coverage.
output: Decision Document: Preserve controller contracts and move billing decisions behind a focused service interface.
Testing Decisions: Protect observable billing outcomes with service and request tests.
Commits: Add characterization tests, extract calculations, extract persistence coordination, switch the controller, and remove obsolete helpers.

best_practices: Provide the business problem, known constraints, and attempted solutions before repository exploration.
Answer implementation questions with concrete examples and identify decisions that remain uncertain.
Review the complete plan and confirm the destination repository before creating the GitHub issue.
anti_patterns: Do not begin with a predetermined solution while withholding relevant constraints.
Do not combine behavior changes, migrations, and cleanup into one large commit.
Do not publish the issue before confirming scope, testing decisions, and excluded work.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes the repository and produces a refactor plan, but it does not implement changes.

faq.question: Will it create a GitHub issue?
faq.answer: Yes, when GitHub access is available. Review the proposed content and repository destination before publication.

faq.question: Why does the skill ask many questions?
faq.answer: The interview resolves scope, constraints, alternatives, interfaces, testing expectations, and implementation decisions before sequencing work.

faq.question: How small are the planned commits?
faq.answer: Each commit should represent one understandable step and leave the codebase in a working state.

faq.question: Does the final issue include file paths?
faq.answer: No. The template excludes file paths and code snippets because they can become outdated.

faq.question: Can it plan a refactor without tests?
faq.answer: It can, but it will identify missing coverage and ask how the affected behavior should be protected.
